summary: 'The design computes an 8-way signed int8 dot product plus a 32-bit bias, multiplies the sum by a 16-bit unsigned
  multiplier, applies a rounding right shift (halves round towards plus infinity) and clamps the result to a signed 8-bit
  value, with an optional ReLU. It sits behind the reusable UART test shell on the Nexys A7-100T (xc7a100tcsg324-1) and
  is driven by register reads and writes over the USB-UART. The run reached simulation level V2 of V3: verification stopped
  at V3 because five cover properties were never hit, so no synthesis, implementation or hardware result exists. The specification
  and architecture were accepted automatically by a model, with no human review.'
scope_not:
- 'Not a general neural-network layer: one 8-element dot product per GO, with no streaming, batching or accumulation across
  calls.'
- 'Not a design with a defined overflow or wrap behaviour: acc overflow and shift outside 1..31 are out of contract and
  untested.'
- Not hardware-verified, not timing-closed and not measured for resources or power; none of those stages ran.

- about: latency_count
  text: 'Counted from rtl/dotq_core.sv and rtl/dotq_regs.sv: with the one-cycle go pulse in cycle 0, v1..v5 follow, done
    is high in cycle 6 and READY is high in cycle 7, so READY rises 7 clocks after the go pulse, or 8 clocks after the shell
    write strobe because dotq_regs registers go. This meets the spec''s "within 8 clocks" only if the count starts at the
    go pulse or the write strobe exactly; it has no margin. ARCHITECTURE.md describes five stages, but the RTL has a sixth
    register stage (the y/acc output register) before done.'
- about: go_priority
  text: 'A GO write always wins over a simultaneous done in dotq_regs.sv (READY ends 0). A new go while a computation is
    in flight also cancels it in dotq_core.sv: every valid stage is gated with ~go, so the earlier result is dropped, and
    the new computation restarts from the loaded operands. Operand writes during a computation are not blocked and can corrupt
    that result; the spec calls this out of contract.'
- about: result_visibility
  text: Y and ACC are not cleared by GO; the core keeps the old values and dotq_regs.sv only masks them to 0 on reads while
    READY is 0. The y/acc registers in the core are overwritten when a computation completes, slightly before READY rises.
- about: unmapped_access
  text: Reads of GO and of every offset above STATUS return 0; writes to the RO registers (Y, ACC, STATUS) and to every
    offset above STATUS are ignored with no error response (dotq_regs.sv default branches). A write to any address other
    than GO never starts a computation. Writes to MULT keep only bits [15:0]; writes to CTRL keep only bits [4:0] and [8].
- about: window_address
  text: 'The register offsets in this document are window-relative. The shell reaches the design only for shell addresses
    with bit 7 set, and the window offset is the low 7 bits (shell_core.sv: win_addr is addr[6:0]), so A_LO is at shell
    address 0x80 and each later register follows at the next address. Shell addresses with bit 7 clear are the shell''s
    own registers (design ID, version, build stamp, scratch, error counters, build ID). A window read returns its data after
    a registered read, one cycle after win_rd.'
- about: ctrl_shift_range
  text: CTRL accepts any 5-bit shift. The RTL handles shift 0 (no rounding constant is added, so the result is the plain
    product) although the spec only defines 1..31. Reset value of shift is 1, of relu 0.

This is a count from the RTL, not a measurement.'
- about: go_priority
  text: 'GO beats completion and an earlier GO. In dotq_regs.sv a GO write in the same cycle as done leaves READY at 0, because the later assignment wins. In dotq_core.sv a new go clears every in-flight pipeline valid bit and suppresses done and the Y/ACC update that cycle, so a GO during a computation restarts it. A GO is always accepted, including when READY is already set.'
- about: operands_not_latched
  text: 'The core reads the operand registers (act, wgt, bias, mult, shift, relu) every clock and does not capture them at GO. Writing any operand or CTRL while a computation is in flight changes the result. The spec assumes this is not required to be safe.'
- about: reserved_accesses
  text: 'Offsets 0x0B-0x7F read 0 and writes to them are ignored (default branches in dotq_regs.sv). GO reads 0, and writes to Y, ACC and STATUS are ignored. The shell still answers every window write with status OK, so the host gets no error for a write to a read-only or unmapped offset.'
- about: read_behaviour
  text: 'Reads have no side effects. Read data is registered in dotq_regs.sv, one cycle after win_rd. Y and ACC read 0 while READY is 0, including after reset and between a GO and completion. MULT bits [31:16] are dropped on write and CTRL bits other than [4:0] and [8] are dropped; both read back as 0. A CTRL write stores shift as written, so shift 0 is accepted, but it is outside the contract and was not tested.'
- about: reset_values
  text: 'Per dotq_regs.sv and dotq_core.sv, reset clears all operand registers, MULT, the go pulse, READY, the core pipeline valid bits, done, y and acc to 0, and sets CTRL to shift 1 and relu 0. The read-data register also resets to 0. The spec says outputs clear within 2 cycles of CPU_RESETN asserting; the RTL clears them on the first clock edge with rst high, and rst is raised asynchronously. This was not measured.'
- about: spec_vs_rtl_names
  text: 'spec.yaml names the LED port LED0 and lists DESIGN_ID as a parameter. The RTL (c14_int8_dot_requant_top.sv) and design.xdc use the port bus LED[0:0] and a localparam DESIGN_ID. The RTL and XDC are what was built; the spec disagrees.'
- about: arithmetic_width
  text: 'dotq_core.sv holds acc*mult as a 49-bit signed value and adds the rounding constant in 50 bits, as the spec requires. The 32-bit acc sum wraps on overflow and nothing saturates it. A weight of -128 is handled, though the spec limits weights to -127..127.'

  text: 'Counted from dotq_regs.sv and dotq_core.sv: the GO write registers a one-cycle go pulse, which then passes through
    six register stages (v1 to v5, then done). Y and ACC are loaded when v5 is set, and READY is set one clock after done.
    The total is inside the spec promise of 8 clocks and READY never rises before Y and ACC are valid. This is a count from
    the RTL, not a measurement.'
- about: go_priority
  text: GO beats completion and an earlier GO. In dotq_regs.sv a GO write in the same cycle as done leaves READY at 0, because
    the later assignment wins. In dotq_core.sv a new go clears every in-flight pipeline valid bit and suppresses done and
    the Y/ACC update that cycle, so a GO during a computation restarts it. A GO is always accepted, including when READY
    is already set.
- about: operands_not_latched
  text: The core reads the operand registers (act, wgt, bias, mult, shift, relu) every clock and does not capture them at
    GO. Writing any operand or CTRL while a computation is in flight changes the result. The spec assumes this is not required
    to be safe.
- about: reserved_accesses
  text: Offsets 0x0B-0x7F read 0 and writes to them are ignored (default branches in dotq_regs.sv). GO reads 0, and writes
    to Y, ACC and STATUS are ignored. The shell still answers every window write with status OK, so the host gets no error
    for a write to a read-only or unmapped offset.
- about: read_behaviour
  text: Reads have no side effects. Read data is registered in dotq_regs.sv, one cycle after win_rd. Y and ACC read 0 while
    READY is 0, including after reset and between a GO and completion. MULT bits [31:16] are dropped on write and CTRL bits
    other than [4:0] and [8] are dropped; both read back as 0. A CTRL write stores shift as written, so shift 0 is accepted,
    but it is outside the contract and was not tested.
- about: reset_values
  text: Per dotq_regs.sv and dotq_core.sv, reset clears all operand registers, MULT, the go pulse, READY, the core pipeline
    valid bits, done, y and acc to 0, and sets CTRL to shift 1 and relu 0. The read-data register also resets to 0. The
    spec says outputs clear within 2 cycles of CPU_RESETN asserting; the RTL clears them on the first clock edge with rst
    high, and rst is raised asynchronously. This was not measured.
- about: spec_vs_rtl_names
  text: spec.yaml names the LED port LED0 and lists DESIGN_ID as a parameter. The RTL (c14_int8_dot_requant_top.sv) and
    design.xdc use the port bus LED[0:0] and a localparam DESIGN_ID. The RTL and XDC are what was built; the spec disagrees.
- about: arithmetic_width
  text: dotq_core.sv holds acc*mult as a 49-bit signed value and adds the rounding constant in 50 bits, as the spec requires.
    The 32-bit acc sum wraps on overflow and nothing saturates it. A weight of -128 is handled, though the spec limits weights
    to -127..127.
